causal-factors.name: Senate inaction / lack of Senate passage
causal-factors.rationale: As of March 1, 2026, H.R. 33 (and its Senate companion S.199) had not clear passage in the Senate, despite House approval, making enactment by May 1, 2026 uncertain.

causal-factors.name: House passage with broad bipartisan support
causal-factors.rationale: H.R. 33 passed the House with a large bipartisan margin (423-1) in January 2025, and a Senate companion was subsequently introduced, signaling sustained legislative momentum.

causal-factors.name: Ongoing US–Taiwan tax negotiations / potential broader framework
causal-factors.rationale: Treasury announced in 2024 that comprehensive tax-relief negotiations with Taiwan would proceed, and later developments (including tariff negotiations in early 2026) could raise pressure to finalize a tax agreement and related enabling legislation.

causal-factors.name: Historical base-rate constraint for federal legislation
causal-factors.rationale: Historical analysis consistently shows only a small fraction of introduced federal bills become law (roughly 5–6%), implying a low baseline probability of enactment by the target date even with momentum.

causal-factors.name: Senate action status and absence of enacted law
causal-factors.rationale: H.R.33 passed the House on January 15, 2025; as of March 1, 2026 there is no enacted law and Senate action has been limited to the referral of S.199 to the Committee on Finance (no final passage), consistent with historically low conversion from House passage to law for cross-border tax bills. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/33/all-info?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Approval and implementing legislation required for entry into force
causal-factors.rationale: The framework adds that entry into force depends on enactment of approval legislation and implementing legislation, creating an additional hurdle beyond regular passage. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/199/text?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Ongoing US–Taiwan tax negotiations and cross-chamber momentum
causal-factors.rationale: Treasury signaled negotiations on a comprehensive tax agreement in 2024, and a Senate companion to H.R.33 was introduced in 2025, signaling continued momentum despite slow progress. ([home.treasury.gov](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy2693?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: House passage and bipartisan support (baseline momentum for action)
causal-factors.rationale: The House passed H.R.33 with broad bipartisan support (423-1) in January 2025, and similar momentum has been noted in concurrent Senate action, raising the odds of eventual enactment. causal-factors.name: Baseline enactment rate for federal legislation (low odds)
causal-factors.rationale: Historical data indicate only about 5–6% of introduced bills become law, implying a consistently low probability even with momentum. ([brookings.edu](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/55426/?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Senate companion introduced (S.199) and cross-chamber attention
causal-factors.rationale: The introduction of S.199 (Senate companion) on January 23, 2025 with multiple cosponsors signals cross-chamber attention that could improve passage prospects if the agenda aligns. causal-factors.name: Senate inaction / slow progress on Senate companion S.199
causal-factors.rationale: As of March 1, 2026, the Senate companion S.199 was introduced on January 23, 2025 but has seen no floor vote or enactment, leaving passage contingent on Senate action (see turn3search0; turn3search1).

causal-factors.name: House passage and Senate companion introduction
causal-factors.rationale: H.R.33 passed the House on January 15, 2025 by a 423-1 vote and a Senate companion was introduced shortly after, signaling ongoing cross-chamber momentum (see turn0search7; turn3search0).

causal-factors.name: Baseline enactment-rate for introduced federal bills
causal-factors.rationale: Historical enactment rates for introduced federal legislation are very low (roughly 5–6%), implying downward pressure on likelihood of enactment (see turn0search7; turn3search7).

causal-factors.name: Ongoing U.S.–Taiwan tax negotiations and potential implementing framework
causal-factors.rationale: Treasury and administration signaled ongoing negotiations toward a comprehensive tax agreement with Taiwan; progress toward a final agreement or implementing legislation could raise odds of enactment (see turn1search3; turn3search8).

synthesis: The House has already passed H.R.33 and a Senate companion exists, suggesting momentum that justifies raising the forecast above the 4% ensemble. However, historical enactment rates and the lack of final Senate passage keep the probability well below a typical success rate, yielding a calibrated outlook around 12% with a wide but plausible range.
